articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Exhibition Explores the 1990s Through Art and Fashion
articles.excerpt: Tate Britain is hosting an exhibition that examines the creative energy and cultural shifts of the 1990s through photography, fashion, and design.
articles.content: Tate Britain is presenting an upcoming exhibition titled The 90s: Art and Fashion, running from 8 October 2026 to 14 February 2027. Curated by Edward Enninful, the exhibition brings together photography, fashion, art, and design to examine a decade defined by cultural shifts and creative experimentation. Visitors can encounter works by artists and photographers such as Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside fashion creations by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. Featured highlights include Mark Leckey's video compilation tracing British dance music culture and Jim Lambie's site-specific floor installations constructed from multi-coloured vinyl tape. The exhibition is free for museum members, and an audio guide featuring insights from curators and artists is available for purchase at an additional cost during ticket booking.

articles.originalTitle: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Roy Lichtenstein Retrospective Opens at the Whitney Museum in New York
articles.excerpt: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, the first retrospective of the artist’s work in New York since 1993, opens at the Whitney Museum of American Art, bringing together roughly 130 works created from the early 1940s through the 1990s.
articles.content: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Roy Lichtenstein: Like New from October 11, 2026, to May 10, 2027. Marking the first retrospective of the artist’s work in New York since 1993, the exhibition traces how Lichtenstein’s early interest in perception and visual recognition shaped a career-long investigation into duplication, simulation, and image culture. Featuring approximately 130 works made from the early 1940s through the 1990s, the exhibition explores how he treated images as unstable forms that could be borrowed, translated, and reframed, illuminating his relationship to copying, influence, appropriation, and the afterlife of images. For the first time, all the works from Lichtenstein’s first exhibition of Pop-style work at Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962 are reunited. This pivotal moment defined an era and extended far beyond Pop, shaping generations of artists whose work is also on view in the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Contemporary Istanbul founder planning new fair on city's Asian side - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: Contemporary Istanbul Founder Planning New Fair on City's Asian Side
articles.excerpt: Turkey's largest contemporary art fair, Contemporary Istanbul, opened its doors for its third year at Tersane Istanbul. Fair founder Ali Güreli announced plans to organize a new event on the Asian side of Istanbul.
articles.content: Turkey's largest contemporary art fair, Contemporary Istanbul, took place for the third consecutive time at the 500-year-old Tersane Istanbul on the Golden Horn, featuring around 70 galleries from over 15 countries. Ali Güreli, the fair's founder and chairman of the board, stated that hosting the entire event on a single floor provided a major advantage. While announcing that the fair will return in 2027 during the same week as the 19th Istanbul Biennial, Güreli also expressed plans to launch a new fair on the Asian side of the city. Additionally, Güreli noted that they are in discussions with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism for an art taxation reform similar to Italy's recent reduction of art acquisition taxes to 5%. This year's programming focused on the Asian market, with participation from centers such as Hong Kong, Tokyo, Seoul, New Delhi, and Singapore. The event also featured the Abu Dhabi-based tech platform Numeraire Future Trends as an official solution partner, offering AI-driven authentication and valuation systems for collectors.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - WWD
articles.title: Patek Philippe Unveils New Timepieces at Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe showcased limited-edition timepieces inspired by the Italian market and new collections at the seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe hosted the seventh and largest edition of its Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan. Staged at CityOval Milano across 31,215 square feet, the exhibition traces the brand's history and contemporary innovations with over 500 items, including the 1868 wristwatch owned by Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Patek Philippe president Thierry Stern noted that Italy represents a long-standing market of connoisseurs. During the event, the manufacturer debuted seven limited-edition timepieces featuring casebacks inscribed with the Milan 2026 detail, including three Calatrava models representing the Italian flag and world-time repeaters depicting downtown Milan. The exhibition also marked the introduction of the Gondolo Ladies First jewelry watch collection. Running through October 18, the event coincides with Milano Watch Week.

articles.originalTitle: New Work: The Long Goodbye by Carrie Mae Weems - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Carrie Mae Weems's New Work on Display at V&A East Museum
articles.excerpt: Carrie Mae Weems's new film The Long Goodbye, commissioned for the opening of V&A East Museum, examines migration and hidden love stories within history.
articles.content: Commissioned for the opening of the V&A East Museum, Carrie Mae Weems's film The Long Goodbye explores migration through the lens of personal love stories intertwined within these journeys. Developed over nearly three years, the work examines how official historical accounts and archives define entrenched narratives, drawing on political debates surrounding migration in both Britain and the United States. Water features prominently in the film as a route of migration and a vessel of history, invoking the transatlantic slave trade and the concept of tidalectics developed by Barbadian poet Kamau Brathwaite. The Long Goodbye is exhibited alongside two archival films by the artist, Before the Loss of You and Okwui, offering visitors a comprehensive look at how love and memory inform her artistic practice and her commitment to making marginalized histories visible.

articles.originalTitle: A Warehouse is Converted Into the New Home for Architecture at MIT - Architectural Record
articles.title: MIT Architecture Department Relocates to Converted Historic Storage Warehouse
articles.excerpt: Gathering architecture, urban planning and design programs, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology has moved into the 19th-century Metropolitan Storage Warehouse building.
articles.content: The architecture department at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology relocated in August to a 195,000-square-foot converted warehouse. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Leers Weinzapfel, the 500-foot-long brick structure includes portions dating back to 1894. The Met Warehouse now houses the department of architecture, the department of urban studies and planning, and the Morningside Academy for Design. To accommodate these programs within the masonry structure, the design strategy involved carving out multistory voids and inserting lightweight structures suspended from the roof to create column-free studio spaces. The conversion pairs these interventions with structural supports, including concrete shear walls and careful steel framing within the masonry. Certain historic elements of the building were reconstructed to meet the requirements of the Cambridge Historical Commission. The completed project establishes a distinct physical home for design disciplines within the scientifically oriented institution.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - Architectural Record
articles.title: East County Library Opens in Oregon Featuring Mass-Timber Architecture
articles.excerpt: Designed by Holst Architecture, the new library in Gresham addresses the growing needs of the region. Spanning 95,000 square feet, the facility cost $163 million to complete.
articles.content: The East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, has opened its doors to serve the growing population and evolving needs of the region. Designed by Holst Architecture, the 95,000-square-foot facility was completed with a total project cost of $163 million. Standing two stories tall yet reaching a height of 59 feet, the building occupies a former light-rail park-and-ride site. The design process incorporated extensive community outreach, involving numerous listening sessions and collaboration with local organizations. Working alongside mass-timber specialist Timberlab, the design team integrated 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels left fully exposed without additional fire-resistant treatments. Interior program elements include open book stacks accommodating 200,000 volumes, a large community auditorium, a recording studio, and specialized rooms for neurodivergent users. Mechanical systems were carefully integrated into the building fabric to maintain clean sightlines across the timber structure.

articles.originalTitle: design museum gent reopens with new wing built from locally made waste bricks - Designboom
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Reopens Following Extensive Four-Year Renovation Project
articles.excerpt: Expanded with a new wing designed by Carmody Groarke and ATAMA, Design Museum Gent features a facade made from locally sourced waste bricks and reopens on October 3, 2026.
articles.content: Design Museum Gent in Belgium reopens on October 3, 2026, following a four-year renovation and expansion led by Carmody Groarke and ATAMA, with historic buildings restored by RE-ST. The project introduces a new 2,200-square-meter wing designed to accommodate exhibitions, workshops, lectures, and community events. A notable architectural feature of the extension is its facade, constructed from over 82,000 Gent Waste Bricks produced locally through a low-energy lime-curing process utilizing municipal waste. The renewed institution launches with an exhibition featuring approximately 500 objects from its collection, organized around contemporary themes such as copy, comfort, and migration rather than traditional chronological order. Another opening exhibition, Public Matter(s): Design and Democracy, examines democratic systems through designed structures and interactive formats. The museum also incorporates AI-powered search tools and collaborative platforms to encourage broader public participation.

articles.originalTitle: São Paulo’s Museu de Arte Moderna reopens after two-year renovation - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: São Paulo Museum of Modern Art Reopens After Two-Year Renovation
articles.excerpt: Having closed its doors for two years of renovations, the São Paulo Museum of Modern Art has reopened with an exhibition designed to push the boundaries of Brazilian art.
articles.content: The Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo (MAM) has resumed operations in its Oscar Niemeyer-designed pavilion in Ibirapuera Park following a two-year closure for renovations. Reopening on 12 September, the institution chose to debut not with its permanent collection, but with the 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art, titled Depois Que Tudo Foi Dito (After It's All Said), running until 24 January 2027. Chief curator Cauê Alves noted the symbolic return to the exact pavilion that hosted the inaugural Panorama in 1969. During the closure, the museum maintained an active profile by organizing over a dozen exhibitions in partner venues. Curated by Diane Lima, the current edition features 33 artists and engages with philosophical perspectives on representation, colonialism and racial violence. Lima explained that the participating artists explore form and materiality rather than fulfilling expected tropes associated with Black, Indigenous and dissident backgrounds. The reopening exhibition serves as a statement on the institution's evolving relationship with its public and artistic boundaries.

articles.originalTitle: Arthur Jafa at the New Museum, Review: A Horror Show for the Ages - artnews.com
articles.title: New Museum Opens Expansive Survey Exhibition Dedicated to Arthur Jafa
articles.excerpt: The New Museum in New York presents "I Am Tony," a major survey exhibition spanning four decades of work by artist Arthur Jafa.
articles.content: The New Museum in New York is presenting "I Am Tony," a major survey exhibition dedicated to the artist Arthur Jafa. On view through January 3, the exhibition spans nearly four decades of Jafa's artistic output across two floors of the museum. Curated by Massimiliano Gioni and Gary Carrion-Murayari, the installation casts much of the gallery space in darkness to highlight Jafa's visual art rather than his cinematic background. The exhibition brings together works ranging from his early binder series Notebooks to the remade automotive sculpture MBD_Trans Am and the computer-generated video AGHDRA. Jafa's perspective that Black existence is intrinsically bound with horror informs much of the presentation, evoking a pervasive sense of danger through recurring motifs of monsters, cinematic appropriations, and unsettling soundscapes. The immersive project underscores the collision of terror and beauty that defines Jafa's oeuvre, offering visitors a nonlinear journey through his influential body of work.

articles.originalTitle: ‘He said the secret to a happy life is attention to the details’: William Morris Gallery reopens after major rehang and restoration - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: William Morris Gallery Reopens Following Major Restoration and Rearrangement
articles.excerpt: The William Morris Gallery in London is reopening to visitors following a comprehensive renovation and rearrangement process on the 130th anniversary of the artist's death.
articles.content: The William Morris Gallery, located in a Grade II-listed manor in Walthamstow, northeast London, where the artist lived as a teenager, is reopening its doors on Saturday, 3 October, following a major renovation and rehang. Marking the first large-scale overhaul since its 2012 redevelopment, the timing coincides with the 130th anniversary of Morris's death. Led by architect Sam Jacob and gallery director Hadrian Garrard, the project aimed to bring a more domestic sensibility to the building. The redevelopment was funded with approximately £1.5m raised from trusts including the Garfield Weston Foundation and the Wolfson Foundation, alongside contributions from the Waltham Forest Council. The revamp transformed six gallery spaces, brought out previously unseen objects, and addressed the complexities and contradictions of Morris's character as both a designer and a socialist activist. The gallery reopens with an exhibition titled 'Earthly Paradise: Radical Living in the UK', exploring radical living spaces in Britain.

articles.originalTitle: Open call: Commissions for English Ceramic Circle Centenary display at V&A South Kensington - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A and English Ceramic Circle Launch Open Call for Centenary Display
articles.excerpt: The English Ceramic Circle has announced plans to commission up to new works for a centenary display at V&A South Kensington, with submissions closing on November 15, 2026.
articles.content: The English Ceramic Circle, the largest and oldest society dedicated to the study of British ceramics and enamels, is marking its 100th anniversary with a special display at V&A South Kensington. Running from October 2027 to September 2028, the exhibition will highlight artistic and technological contributions from potters working in Britain from 1600 to the present. To support this display, the circle is seeking to commission up to three new works through an open submission process aimed at UK-based ceramic artists. Organizers particularly encourage proposals from early- and mid-career practitioners with between 3 and 15 years of experience working with clay. Selected artists will receive a fee of 3,000 pounds per artist and will work alongside curatorial staff to develop their projects. Finished works must be delivered to the museum by September 2027 for exhibition in Room 146. Applications require a 300-word artist statement and a 500-word proposal detailing the idea, physical form, dimensions, and materials. The deadline for submissions is November 15, 2026, with successful applicants notified in December 2026. The acquired works will ultimately be donated to a public museum in the UK following the conclusion of the display.

articles.originalTitle: JUUL. Transformation of the Julianakerk / HA-HA Design & Development - ArchDaily
articles.title: Julianakerk Church in Rotterdam Converted Into Residential Project
articles.excerpt: Nine years after a devastating fire, the remains of the Julianakerk church in Rotterdam have been transformed into four homes under the JUUL residential project in Heijplaat.
articles.content: The remains of the Julianakerk church in the Rotterdam garden village of Heijplaat have been transformed into a residential development nine years after a severe fire damaged the structure. Led by HA-HA Design & Development, the JUUL project converted the fire-damaged remains into four distinct homes across a 700-square-meter area, bringing renewed purpose to a site that had stood vacant and impaired for years. Structural engineering for the adaptive reuse project was provided by IMd raadgevende ingenieurs, while LBP Sight oversaw environmental sustainability and building physics. BIK Bouw served as the general contractor for the construction phase. The initiative integrates modern residential architecture within the conserved framework of the historic church structure. Lighting design for the development was coordinated by RMBK, and the landscape architecture was also handled by the lead design firm. The completed project restores a damaged local landmark while adding new residential capacity to the Heijplaat district through careful preservation and structural intervention.

articles.originalTitle: The Luxembourg Pavilion Examines Overconsumption of Living Space Through "Excess!" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale - ArchDaily
articles.title: Luxembourg Pavilion to Examine Living Space Consumption at 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
articles.excerpt: The Luxembourg Pavilion at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale will address the overconsumption and inequitable distribution of living space through a curatorial proposal titled 'Excess!'
articles.content: A jury of arts and architecture professionals announced the selected curatorial proposal for the Luxembourg Pavilion at the Biennale Architettura 2027. Titled 'Excess! On the Overconsumption of Living Space,' the exhibition is curated by housing expert Céline Zimmer alongside architects Bùi Quý Sơn and Paul-Antoine Lucas, co-founders of Exutoire. The proposal addresses the inequitable distribution of living space as a reflection of broader habits contributing to current housing and ecological crises. The issue will be illustrated through a dialogue between the realities of Luxembourg and Vietnam to reflect on spatial consumption. Located on the first floor of the Sale d'Armi in the Arsenale, the Luxembourg Pavilion will open to the public on May 8, 2027. The curatorial team draws on professional experience in housing systems, social justice through design, and queer theory in architecture to open up conversations and learn from intersecting perspectives. The upcoming Venice Architecture Biennale will run from May 8 to November 21, 2027, featuring the overarching theme 'Do Architecture — For the Possibility of Coexistence Facing a Real Reality,' curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu.

articles.originalTitle: Christine Sun Kim, Rodney McMillian, Vincent Valdez Win MacArthur ‘Genius’ Grants - ARTnews.com
articles.title: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation Announces 2026 'Genius Grant' Recipients
articles.excerpt: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation has announced the 20 recipients of its annual MacArthur Fellowships, commonly known as genius grants. Each fellow receives 800000 dollars in unrestricted funds as part of the program.
articles.content: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation has released the names of the 20 recipients chosen for its annual MacArthur Fellowships, colloquially known as genius grants. The distinction comes with 800000 dollars in unrestricted funds for each recipient. The 2026 cohort features four artists among its members: Christine Sun Kim, Rodney McMillian, Vincent Valdez, and Chip Thomas. Based in Berlin, Christine Sun Kim creates works that challenge institutional ableism and examine the lived realities of Deaf people. Rodney McMillian explores how history, socioeconomic conditions, and public policy shape life quality, particularly regarding the economic marginalization of Black Americans. Vincent Valdez focuses on racism and the Latinx experience through painting. Chip Thomas transforms overlooked spaces into community-grounded public art projects, frequently working within the Navajo Nation. According to foundation communications, the fellows continue a tradition of defying boundaries, questioning conventions, and expanding the scope of human inquiry through their respective disciplines.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces exhibitors and showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach Edition - artbasel.com
articles.title: Art Basel Announces Exhibitor Lineup for Miami Beach 2026 Edition
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach has announced that its 2026 edition will feature 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries alongside a reconfigured showfloor.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach has announced the exhibitor lineup and program highlights for its 2026 edition, taking place from December 4 to 6 at the Miami Beach Convention Center, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3. The fair will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories. Responding to feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee, the 2026 show features a substantially reconfigured floor plan that occupies approximately 12 percent less space, while the main Galleries sector hosts roughly 10 percent fewer exhibitors distributed across four hospitality plazas. The fair comprises four sectors—Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey—alongside the digital art initiative Zero 10. More than two-thirds of the participating galleries operate spaces in the Americas, with Brazil forming the third-largest national contingent. Additional programs include an outdoor presentation by James Turrell and a participatory exhibition by Public Art Fund in Collins Park, alongside the return of the Art Basel Awards in partnership with BOSS.

articles.originalTitle: Digital Art Committee - Centre Pompidou
articles.title: Centre Pompidou Establishes Five-Year Digital Art Committee
articles.excerpt: The Centre Pompidou has announced the establishment of a Digital Art Committee for a five-year period to support digital art, fund acquisitions, and contribute to research programmes.
articles.content: The Centre Pompidou has established a Digital Art Committee bringing together French and international patrons to support the institution's commitment to digital art and raise its profile in this area. Operating for five years, the programme will fund the acquisition of works for the Centre Pompidou - Musée National d'Art Moderne collection, support promotion and sharing policies for digital art, and back conservation operations on artworks. The initiative continues the institution's history with computer-assisted creation, following the 1975 establishment of the Studio of Research in Advanced Techniques. In 2023, the institution became the first modern and contemporary art museum to acquire a set of works related to the blockchain. In recent years, the new media collection has also acquired its first works using virtual reality and augmented reality. Furthermore, a partnership with KADIST has fostered reflections around artificial intelligence, leading to several acquisitions in this area. During this period, the museum carried out research into the earliest decades of computer-assisted creation, adding works from the 1960s to the 1990s to its collection.

articles.originalTitle: David Bowie’s unrealised projects - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Explores Unrealised Projects in David Bowie Archive
articles.excerpt: Archival scripts, drawings and notes housed at the Victoria and Albert Museum reveal the creative process behind David Bowie's unproduced projects, including Nineteen Eighty-Four, Diamond Dogs and Young Americans.
articles.content: David Bowie worked on multiple projects across various mediums throughout his career, though some were never fully realised in his lifetime. The David Bowie Archive at the Victoria and Albert Museum contains film scripts, storyboards, lyrics and research notes from these unproduced works. Between 1973 and 1974, Bowie and director Tony Ingrassia devised a musical-comedy adaptation of George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four. Although the musical was not realised, its themes continued into the Diamond Dogs album and project. The archive also preserves handwritten notes, plot summaries and drawings for Bowie's Young Americans film project, the television production The Catastrophy Cabinet, and All The Emperor's Horses, a planned collaboration about the Chinese Communist Revolution. Additionally, materials related to Derek Jarman and Lee Drysdale's apocalyptic science fiction film Neutron, in which Bowie was cast as a lead role, document the extensive creative worlds developed across his career.

articles.originalTitle: 12 uplifting design stories we discovered in Finland this month - wallpaper.com
articles.title: Helsinki Design Week Showcases Urban Innovation and Creative Growth in Finland
articles.excerpt: Helsinki Design Week highlighted innovative urban design projects, circular architecture, and collaborative creative strategies across the Finnish capital this September.
articles.content: Held in September, Helsinki Design Week brought together innovative design approaches aimed at enhancing urban habitats and everyday life. A strategic planning document commissioned by the City of Helsinki's Economic Development Division outlined nine key actions for growing the creative sectors alongside urban development. During the event, architect Pekka Airaxin launched Kainuu, a new company delivering turnkey summer houses constructed from cross-laminated timber sourced from managed forests within an 80 km radius. Kainuu has already delivered 10 houses, with 20 more in the pipeline. Additionally, Finnish architect and theorist Juhanni Pallasmaa donated his entire 10,000-strong book collection to Helsinki's Architecture & Design Museum in honor of his 90th birthday, with 10 percent of the collection currently on display at a temporary space. Hotel refurbishments and material-led experimental projects further highlighted the city's ongoing design engagement.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Surrey Quays and Northolt Stations Complete Accessibility Upgrades in London
articles.excerpt: London transport network stations Surrey Quays and Northolt have introduced new step-free access routes, lifts, and footbridges to improve journeys for wheelchair users and passengers with luggage.
articles.content: London transport infrastructure has been updated with step-free access improvements at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations, facilitating travel for wheelchair users, older residents, and parents with pushchairs. Transport for London reported that Surrey Quays on the London Overground now features an accessible entrance, ticket hall, footbridge, stairs, and lifts connecting both platforms, alongside baby changing and accessible toilet facilities. Funded partially through the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government alongside developer contributions, the Surrey Quays project utilized low-carbon CEM 3 concrete, electric arc furnace steel, and glue-laminated timber beams to minimize carbon impact. Construction engineering involved complex temporary works near 19th-century retaining walls, utilizing lightweight foam blocks to distribute loads safely. At Northolt station on the Central line, a new footbridge and lift system were installed between the street level and platforms at an estimated cost of 15.3 million pounds, making it the 95th station on the Tube network to offer step-free access. The Northolt upgrades also incorporated embankment regrading and replanting with native trees to support local biodiversity net gain.

articles.originalTitle: Basquiat, the Blue Ribbon Paintings, and the Art of Reproduction | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Princeton University Art Museum Exhibits Jean-Michel Basquiat’s Blue Ribbon Paintings
articles.excerpt: The Princeton University Art Museum has announced an exhibition examining Jean-Michel Basquiat's radical engagement with reproductive media, bringing together eleven Blue Ribbon paintings from 1984 alongside his known print projects.
articles.content: The Princeton University Art Museum in New Jersey is organizing an exhibition exploring Jean-Michel Basquiat's radical engagement with reproductive media from October 4, 2026, to January 31, 2027. At the center of the exhibition are the artist's Blue Ribbon paintings, eleven lesser-known works from 1984 featuring densely layered imagery such as anatomical diagrams, film logos, and crowned figures. The show examines Basquiat's connections with other artists and pioneering Black printmakers, revealing a lineage of Black experimentation and intergenerational exchange within reproductive media. By assembling nearly all of the artist's known print projects, the exhibition frames Basquiat as a conceptual artist probing identity, reproduction, and visibility within an increasingly commercialized art world. The broader cultural context also features developments such as Adriana Varejão's preparations to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia and ongoing artistic initiatives curated by figures like Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu for upcoming international exhibitions.

articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Rick Lowe Exhibition Opens at University of Michigan Museum of Art
articles.excerpt: Black Wall Street Journey, Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027.
articles.content: Rick Lowe's public art project Black Wall Street Journey has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art as the artist's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States. On view in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027, the exhibition brings together painting, sculpture, and public installation to examine how Black prosperity, resilience, and self-determination are represented, measured, and understood. The presentation reflects the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the institution and mirrors his deep engagement with researchers, data scientists, and numerous students. Working collaboratively across art, data, and inquiry, Lowe examines the forces that shape Black wealth and opportunity, ranging from income and education to housing and business ownership.

articles.originalTitle: Glenn Brown in: Fail We May, Sail We Must | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Works from the Brown Collection on View in London
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition brings together artworks spanning six centuries at the Brown Collection in London.
articles.content: Curated by Glenn Brown and his husband Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition titled Fail We May, Sail We Must is on view at the Brown Collection through August 7, 2027. The presentation features paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics by more than twenty artists spanning six centuries, incorporating spliced collages, double images, and elongated figures. The exhibition aims to challenge the mechanisms of the mind and create connections between works not typically seen together. Additionally, the Fall 2026 issue of Gagosian Quarterly has been published, coinciding with a catalogue raisonné and exhibition dedicated to Brice Marden. In other developments, Adriana Varejão opened her studio to share her working practice as she prepares new works to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia. Curated by Diane Lima, the Brazilian Pavilion features Varejão alongside Rosana Paulino, reflecting on colonial narratives and history.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collections and Designs Presented at Paris Design Week 2026
articles.excerpt: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week featured contemporary furniture, lighting, and decor collections rooted in traditional techniques and natural forms.
articles.content: Paris Design Week marked its 16th edition across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond with 500 exhibitors. Draga and Aurel showcased Crisalide side tables featuring fused colored glass and brass bases, while Pinto teamed up with Nobilis to present the warm-toned Foundation collection. Yves Salomon Éditions introduced Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior range inspired by natural forms. Swedish design house Veermakers opened a new showroom in Le Marais, and Nordic Knots presented wool rugs influenced by Swedish Grace. L'Objet partnered with jeweler Jessica McCormack for sea-inspired tabletop objects. Modern Metier exhibited Rudy Guénaire's Tropic of Capricorn collection, and Garnier & Linker unveiled Aurora, an outdoor lighting series. Franck Genser presented his Piscine VI coffee table, and wood-working atelier Hervet Manufacturier displayed its full furniture range during the design week.
